title: Smooth coefficient opens of the explicit polynomial standardizer
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a finitely presented commutative $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and $B$ a commutative algebra over $k$ and $A$ with compatible scalar towers. Let $d,s,N$ be natural numbers with $N>0$, and $a:\operatorname{Fin}(s)\to A$ satisfy $(a_j)_j=H_{A/k}$, the singular ideal [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]. Put $S=k[x_0,\ldots,x_{d-1}]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and give $B$ a compatible $S$-algebra structure. Suppose $P$ is an $A$-presentation of $B$ on variables $x_i,z_{ij}$ and relations indexed by $\operatorname{Fin}(d)$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], with $P(x_i)$ the image of $X_i\in S$ and relations $x_i^{2N}-\sum_j z_{ij}a_j$. Then for every $j$, $B[1/a_j]$ is smooth over $S$ [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

source.place: Proof of Lemma 07FJ, Ad item-strictly-standard: elimination on the coefficient opens

proof.text: The finite presentation of A over k and the finite quotient presentation of B over A imply that B is finite type over k and hence over S=k[x]. Since S is Noetherian, B is finitely presented over S, as is its principal localization L=B[1/a_j]. The generator a_j lies in singularIdeal k A, so A[1/a_j] is smooth over k.

Apply the square-zero lifting criterion to L over S. For a given map L to T/I with I^2=0, the coefficient map A to T/I extends to A[1/a_j], because a_j maps to a unit. Lift that coefficient map using its smoothness over k. This gives alpha:A to T with alpha(a_j) invertible and the required reduction.

Choose lifts z_il in T of the auxiliary generator images. Put epsilon_i = image(X_i)^(2N) - sum_l z_il alpha(a_l). Evaluating the original relation shows epsilon_i maps to zero in T/I. Replace z_ij by z_ij+epsilon_i alpha(a_j)^(-1), leaving every other z_il unchanged. The sum increases by exactly epsilon_i, so all defining relations hold. Every generator still has the original image in T/I. The quotient presentation universal property gives a ring map B to T. It is an S-algebra map because its x_i-images were fixed by S, and extends to L because alpha(a_j) is a unit. Verify the reduction on coefficients and variables, then use the surjectivity of the presentation and localization uniqueness. This completes the lifting property and thus smoothness.

lean.statement:
theorem popescu_standardizer_coefficient_smooth
    {k : Type u} {A : Type v} {B : Type t}
    [Field k] [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra k A] [Algebra k B]
    [Algebra A B] [IsScalarTower k A B]
    [FinitePresentation k A] {d s : ℕ} (N : ℕ) (_hN : 0 < N)
    (a : Fin s → A) (ha : Ideal.span (Set.range a) = singularIdeal k A)
    [Algebra (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) B]
    [IsScalarTower k (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) B]
    (P : Presentation A B (Fin d ⊕ (Fin d × Fin s)) (Fin d))
    (hval : ∀ i, P.val (Sum.inl i) =
      algebraMap (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k) B (MvPolynomial.X i))
    (hrel : ∀ i : Fin d, P.relation i =
      (MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inl i)) ^ (2 * N) -
        ∑ j : Fin s, MvPolynomial.X (Sum.inr (i, j)) * MvPolynomial.C (a j)) :
    ∀ j, Smooth (MvPolynomial (Fin d) k)
      (Localization.Away (algebraMap A B (a j)))
